meta.title: Contoso Insurance - Claims Platform Migration Weekly Client Call

discussion_points: The original go‑live date of 30 April is no longer achievable due to a defect in the transformation logic.
Claims with multiple linked policies lose secondary policy links during migration, affecting about 41,000 records.
UAT cannot commence until the defect is fixed, leaving 23 scripts and 11 testers idle.
The vendor’s document storage API is overdue, with the latest commitment set for 27 March.
A new go‑live date of 29 May is proposed, contingent on a clean rehearsal by 27 March.

lines.text: Contoso Insurance - Claims Platform Migration
Weekly Client Call
Date: 12 March 2026
Attendees: Priya Nair (Delivery Manager), Raj Menon (Solution Architect), Elena Fischer (Test Manager), Diane Okafor (Contoso, Programme Director), Bill Hartley (Contoso, Head of Claims Ops)

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Thanks for joining. I want to be straight with you today rather than walk through a status deck.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: The go-live date of the thirtieth of April is no longer achievable. I will explain why and what we are proposing.

lines.speaker: Diane Okafor
lines.text: I appreciate the directness. Go on.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Three things have converged. Raj, do you want to cover the migration defect?

lines.speaker: Raj Menon
lines.text: Yes. During the second dress rehearsal we found that claims with more than one linked policy migrate with the policy links dropped.

lines.speaker: Raj Menon
lines.text: The claim record arrives, the financials are correct, but the link back to the secondary policy is gone.

lines.speaker: Bill Hartley
lines.text: How many claims does that affect?

lines.speaker: Raj Menon
lines.text: About nine percent of the historical set. Roughly forty one thousand records.

lines.speaker: Bill Hartley
lines.text: That is not a rounding error. Those are our complex claims, the ones that matter most.

lines.speaker: Raj Menon
lines.text: Agreed. It is a defect in the transformation logic, not the data. We can fix it, but every fix has to be followed by a full rehearsal to prove it.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: And a full rehearsal is a five day cycle.

lines.speaker: Elena Fischer
lines.text: That is the second problem. UAT cannot start while this is open. We would be testing against data we know is wrong.

lines.speaker: Elena Fischer
lines.text: We have twenty three UAT scripts ready and eleven testers booked from Contoso's side. They are effectively idle.

lines.speaker: Diane Okafor
lines.text: Those testers were released from their day roles specifically for this window.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: I know, and I am sorry. Holding them idle is not acceptable, so we need to agree a new window today.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: The third issue is the vendor. Raj?

lines.speaker: Raj Menon
lines.text: The document storage API from the vendor was due on the twenty eighth of February. It is still not delivered.

lines.speaker: Raj Menon
lines.text: Their latest commitment is the twenty seventh of March, which is the third date they have given us.

lines.speaker: Diane Okafor
lines.text: Is that contract ours or yours?

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: It is a Contoso contract. We have no leverage with them directly.

lines.speaker: Diane Okafor
lines.text: Then I will escalate it. I will speak to their account director this week.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Diane to escalate the document storage API delay with the vendor account director this week.

lines.speaker: Bill Hartley
lines.text: What is the new go-live date?

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: We are proposing the twenty ninth of May. That assumes the transformation fix lands by the twenty seventh of March and the fourth rehearsal is clean.

lines.speaker: Elena Fischer
lines.text: And UAT moving to a four week window starting the sixth of April.

lines.speaker: Diane Okafor
lines.text: A month's slip. I have to take that to the executive committee on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Diane Okafor
lines.text: What I need from you is a written note by Monday setting out the cause, the recovery plan and what changes so this does not happen a third time.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Priya to provide a written recovery note to Diane by Monday 16 March.

lines.speaker: Raj Menon
lines.text: I will own the transformation fix. Target is the twenty seventh of March for the fix and the rehearsal.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Raj to deliver the multi-policy transformation fix and a clean rehearsal by 27 March.

lines.speaker: Elena Fischer
lines.text: I will rework the UAT plan for the April window and reconfirm the tester bookings.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Elena to reissue the UAT plan for the 6 April window by 20 March.

lines.speaker: Bill Hartley
lines.text: I want to say something about confidence. This is the second slip. The first one we were told about a week after the fact.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: That is fair criticism and it is on me.

lines.speaker: Diane Okafor
lines.text: Let us focus on recovery. I would rather have an honest May date than an optimistic April one.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Understood. Anything else from your side?

lines.speaker: Diane Okafor
lines.text: No. Send the note by Monday. I have to drop, I have another call.

lines.speaker: Bill Hartley
lines.text: Same here. Thanks both.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Thanks Diane, thanks Bill.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Right, they have gone. Let us have two minutes internally.

lines.speaker: Elena Fischer
lines.text: That went better than I expected.

lines.speaker: Raj Menon
lines.text: Honestly their team never reviews anything on time. Half of those forty one thousand records would not be an issue if they had signed off the mapping document in January like they promised.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: That is true but it is not going in the note. We own the transformation logic.

lines.speaker: Elena Fischer
lines.text: We should also be honest that we sized the rehearsal cycle wrong. Five days was always optimistic.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Agreed. I will put the rehearsal sizing in the lessons learned.

lines.speaker: Raj Menon
lines.text: One risk nobody said out loud on the call. If the fourth rehearsal is not clean, May is gone too.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: That is the real risk. Let us log it.

lines.speaker: Elena Fischer
lines.text: And we are one architect deep on the transformation logic. If Raj is unavailable in the next three weeks we have a problem.

lines.speaker: Priya Nair
lines.text: Also going in the log. Thanks both.

documents.mom_markdown:
## Attendees
- Priya Nair
- Raj Menon
- Elena Fischer
- Diane Okafor
- Bill Hartley

## Agenda
- Status of migration defect
- Impact on UAT schedule
- Vendor API delivery delay
- New go‑live date proposal
- Recovery plan and action items

## Key discussion points
- The original go‑live date of 30 April is no longer achievable due to a defect in the transformation logic.
- Claims with multiple linked policies lose secondary policy links during migration, affecting about 41,000 records.
- UAT cannot commence until the defect is fixed, leaving 23 scripts and 11 testers idle.
- The vendor’s document storage API is overdue, with the latest commitment set for 27 March.
- A new go‑live date of 29 May is proposed, contingent on a clean rehearsal by 27 March.

## Decisions
- The new go‑live date is proposed as 29 May.
- UAT will move to a four‑week window starting 6 April.

## Action items
- Priya Nair will provide a written recovery note to Diane Okafor by Monday 16 March.
- Raj Menon will deliver the multi‑policy transformation fix and a clean rehearsal by 27 March.
- Elena Fischer will reissue the UAT plan for the 6 April window by 20 March.

## Overall status: Red
The go‑live date of 30 April is no longer achievable, causing a milestone slip.

## Summary
The migration defect in transformation logic has prevented the original go‑live date and impacted UAT readiness. A new go‑live date of 29 May has been proposed.

## Progress this period
- The defect affecting 41,000 records has been identified.
- A new go‑live date of 29 May and a four‑week UAT window starting 6 April have been agreed.

## Next steps
- Priya Nair will submit a written recovery note to Diane Okafor by 16 March.
- Raj Menon will deliver the multi‑policy transformation fix and a clean rehearsal by 27 March.
- Elena Fischer will reissue the UAT plan for the 6 April window by 20 March.

## Risks and issues
- The go‑live date of 30 April is no longer achievable.
- Claims with more than one linked policy migrate with the policy links dropped.
- About nine percent of the historical set, roughly forty one thousand records, are affected by the defect.
- The defect is in the transformation logic and must be fixed with a full rehearsal to prove it.

## Support needed from the client
None at this time.
